label: Processed cheese
note: Made from whatever natural cheese the maker has: mostly Cheddar and Colby in the US, Emmental or Gouda types in Europe, and fresh curd for Cancoillotte and requeijão

about.text: Processed cheese is a product made from cheese mixed with an emulsifying agent. Additional ingredients, such as unfermented dairy ingredients, salt, vegetable oils, sugar, or food coloring may be included. As a result, many flavors, colors, and textures of processed cheese exist. Processed cheese typically contains around 50–60% cheese and 40–50% other ingredients.

how.text: Natural cheese is ground and heated with emulsifying salts into a smooth, uniform mass. The US standard (21 CFR 133) requires at least 65.6 °C for 30 seconds; the EU and Germany set no such figure, and factories usually melt hotter, around 80–95 °C, for a few minutes.

steps.note: With emulsifying salts (phosphates, citrates, tartrates) up to 3 % of the weight, and factories usually melt at about 80–95 °C for a few minutes.
